Business data map

How Bunkai works under the hood. Sources: ../upex-bunkai-tms at origin/staging (98ee1b4), the live database through DBHub (read-only, 2026-10-11), and the maps business-domain-context (vocabulary) and infra-context (architecture). Paths are relative to the target repo.

Overview

Bunkai is a multi-tenant Test Management System that puts QA discipline into the data model: an ATC cannot exist without an Acceptance Criterion of its own User Story, and Runs and Bugs carry the ATC they came from. The core mechanic is ATC reuse: one ATC, chained by many Tests, edited once. Around it sit execution (Runs with per-step verdicts), native defects, Test Plans, Jira import, notifications, billing, and workspace lifecycle (export, deletion).

Actors: workspace roles owner > admin > member > viewer; AI agents and CI through PATs; three system actors: pg_cron (run sweep, workspace purge), Vercel Cron (email digest) and Stripe (billing webhook).

Invariants live in Postgres: named bunkai_* RPCs (raising 45xxx SQLSTATEs) and RLS policies, not app-layer services. One Supabase project serves local, staging and production.

Key relationships

  • Workspace owns members, invites, projects, tests, runs, bugs, test plans, exports and checkout sessions; RLS on every child chains back to workspace membership.
  • Project owns modules, environments, stories, ATCs, runs, bugs, milestones, test plans and import jobs.
  • User Story has ACs; ATC binds to ACs of its own story (many-to-many); Test chains ATCs through test_steps (many-to-many, repeats allowed).
  • Run = one Test on one Environment; run_atcs snapshot each chain position, run_steps each ATC step.
  • Bug anchors to a Module and optionally the ATC, Run and Run Step it failed on.
  • Test Plan references Tests (at most once per plan); removing a membership never touches the Test.

Vocabulary, UI labels and enum values: bun run context:map business-domain-context. Columns: query the DB on demand.

Run snapshots vs live ATCs

Two guarantees would conflict without snapshots: an ATC edit propagates to every Test that chains it, and past Run results never change. A Run therefore freezes each position (run_atcs.atc_title, step content in run_steps) at start. Tests read the live ATC; Runs read their snapshot. A test that edits an ATC and then reads an old Run must see the OLD title.

Workspace soft delete and paid seats

workspaces.deleted_at set means the workspace is gone for everyone, owner included, though rows still exist until the purge. Helper functions used by RLS and RPCs ignore deleted workspaces since migration 0089 (BK-991): every child entity must answer as not found. purchased_seats is NULL until a paid upgrade; the webhook writes it.

Flow: sign up and create a workspace

  1. User authenticates (password, magic link, GitHub or Google).
  2. No active membership: redirect to /onboarding.
  3. POST /api/v1/workspaces with name and slug creates the workspace (plan community) and an active owner membership in one bootstrap RPC.
  4. Redirect to /projects.

Rules: slug unique; creator becomes owner; owner is never granted by invite.

Flow: author a story and anchor an ATC

  1. Create a User Story (title 3-200, Markdown, optional Jira key, unique per project).
  2. Add ordered Acceptance Criteria.
  3. Mark ready_to_test: needs at least one active AC, else 45010.
  4. Create the ATC with steps, assertions, layer, tags (max 10, 45024), optional technique and priority, and a non-empty AC set from the same story (else 45020). Story, ATC and links are written atomically.
  5. Editing the ATC bumps its version and propagates to chaining Tests.

Flow: compose a Test and execute a Run

  1. Build a Test from the workspace ATC library (ordered chain, reorder by chain step id).
  2. Start a run on a Project Environment: runs row running, snapshot rows pending.
  3. Runner marks each step passed / failed / blocked / skipped; last write wins while running; Realtime pushes updates.
  4. Finish recomputes the verdict (passed or failed) or Abort with a reason (aborted). Marking a closed run fails (45212).
  5. Side effects: activity_log rows fan out to run.finished / run.aborted notifications; idle runs are auto-aborted by the sweep.

Flow: file a bug from a failed step

  1. "Report bug" appears only for member+ on a failed step.
  2. Dialog pre-fills title, severity P3, repro steps from the executed step, evidence links (http/https, max 10).
  3. POST /api/v1/bugs re-checks the step is still failed (422 run_step_not_failed).
  4. Bug created open, anchored to module, ATC, run, step; consistency trigger checks anchors share the project.
  5. Assign (active non-viewer only) and advance status one step at a time; each change notifies the assignee.

Flow: invite and accept

  1. Admin or owner issues an invite (email + viewer/member/admin); a hashed secret is stored.
  2. Invitee opens /invites/accept?token=… and accepts via POST /api/v1/invites/accept.
  3. Accept upserts the membership; never demotes an existing equal-or-higher role.
  4. Expired, revoked, never-issued, or invites of a deleted workspace all answer the same 404 "Invite token is invalid." (BK-988).

Flow: import stories from Jira

  1. POST /api/v1/imports with project and JQL (member+, atc:write); second active import on the project is 409 import_in_progress (partial unique index).
  2. Row queued; Vercel after() worker claims it atomically (running); client polls every 2 s.
  3. Per issue: ADF to Markdown (50 KB cap), extract ACs, route to the first matching Jira component's module or an auto-created "Inbox", upsert the story by external_id (update keeps module and status), append only new AC titles.
  4. Per-issue errors go to errors[]; job ends completed, or failed on a fatal error (e.g. jira_unauthorized).

Flow: manage a Test Plan

  1. Create in a project via bunkai_create_test_plan (actor is auth.uid(), no actor parameter): name 1-100 (45600), description up to 500 (45601), goal up to 100 (45602); whitespace normalized, name unique case-insensitively.
  2. Update while open; a closed plan refuses edits (45603).
  3. Add Tests: non-empty selection (45605), Tests from the plan's project only (45604), duplicates rejected by unique index (23505); also guarded by the Idempotency-Key header.
  4. Remove a Test: deletes the membership only.

Writes: only through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs; test_plan_tests has SELECT-only RLS.

Flow: upgrade to the Cloud plan

  1. POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout with seat quantity and an Idempotency-Key; PAT callers get a distinguishable rejection (BK-828).
  2. A billing_checkout_sessions row (open, target cloud) is inserted BEFORE calling Stripe; its id is the Stripe client_reference_id. A partial unique index allows one open session per workspace.
  3. User pays on Stripe hosted Checkout; cancel route closes the session as canceled.
  4. Stripe posts to the webhook: checkout.session.completed / async_payment_succeeded set workspaces.plan = 'cloud' and purchased_seats and complete the session; async_payment_failed / expired release the lock. Other event types answer 200 ignored. Events are deduped by id in stripe_webhook_events.

Project limit: a trigger on projects insert refuses a new project at the tier limit (community 3, cloud 50, enterprise unlimited, unknown plan most restrictive) with 45700 project_limit_reached.

Flow: export workspace data

  1. Owner, on a cookie session, requests an export; insert policy enforces owner; one active export per workspace.
  2. Insert trigger writes an export.requested activity row.
  3. Vercel after() worker (service role) builds the archive into Supabase Storage: queued to running to completed (expires in 168 h) or failed with error_message.
  4. Download re-checks owner + completed + unexpired on every request, streams the file (no signed URL) and writes export.downloaded.

Flow: delete and restore a workspace

  1. Owner requests deletion (non-owner 45900, already deleted 45901).
  2. One transaction sets deleted_at and deletion_requested_by and writes a workspace_deletions tombstone (name, slug, member count, row-count digest, purge deadline now + 30 days).
  3. Access ends immediately for every member; every entity of the workspace answers as not found.
  4. Owner may restore during grace (deleted_at = null, no data movement; 45902 if not deleted).
  5. Daily purge (03:00 UTC) hard-deletes workspaces past the deadline; the tombstone stays with purged_at.

Flow: daily email digest

  1. Vercel Cron calls POST /api/v1/admin/send-digest at 08:00 UTC with the CRON_SECRET bearer (401 otherwise).
  2. bunkai_notification_digest_candidates() returns users with unread notifications and email enabled.
  3. The route renders titles and links with the inbox's own vocabulary and sends through Resend.
  4. One notification_digest_log row per user per day (pending, sent, failed) prevents a second send the same day.

Integration: Supabase

Database, auth, RLS, Realtime (Runner updates), Storage (export archives) and pg_cron. Every flow depends on it. The service-role client (RLS bypassed) is used by the import and export workers, the idempotency ledger and PAT secrets. If Supabase is down, nothing works. One project for all environments: test data is production-adjacent.

Integration: Stripe

Outbound: checkout session creation. Inbound: signed webhook. Data impact: workspaces.plan, purchased_seats, billing_checkout_sessions, stripe_webhook_events. If Stripe is down: checkout fails and no plan changes; a session row stays open until an expiry event arrives, which blocks a new checkout for that workspace.

Integration: Resend

Outbound only, digest emails. Data impact: notification_digest_log. If Resend is down: rows end failed; the in-app inbox is unaffected.

Integration: Jira (customer import)

Outbound pull by JQL; Jira never calls Bunkai. Data impact: user_stories, acceptance_criteria, modules (auto "Inbox"), import_jobs. Backoff on 429. Bad credentials fail the job, not the app. Distinct from this QA repo's own jira:sync-issues.

Integration: Vercel

Hosts the app, runs after() workers (import, export) and the digest cron. A worker killed mid-run leaves a job running; the claim is atomic but no sweep exists for import or export jobs.

Discovery gaps

  • No figures: tables and text carry every fact; the system architecture figure lives in infra-context (architecture). Draw a section figure only where a picture adds mechanism.
  • cron.job is not readable by qa_inspector_ro; schedules taken from migrations 0075 and 0084, not from the live scheduler.
  • Test Plan close: no close RPC in 0073 or 0076, yet closed is a valid status; how a plan is closed is unverified.
  • Who may start a billing checkout (owner only?) not verified in code.
  • Stuck running import or export jobs after a worker crash: no sweep found.
  • ready_to_test to draft reverse guard not verified.
  • Run abort and finish SQLSTATE ranges beyond 45212 and 45215 not enumerated.
  • Jira import edge cases: multiple matching components, near-duplicate AC titles on re-import.
  • Retention (30 / 90 days per tier) is displayed but no pruning job exists.
